summary: Unlock the power of R programming for statistical computing. Join our training course to gain essential skills for data analysis and decision-making.
lede: R Programming for Statistical Computing teaches you to move from raw, structured, or unstructured data to validated analysis using R, tidyverse tools, statistical models, visualizations, and reproducible reports. You will practice importing and transforming data, exploring distributions with ggplot2, diagnosing models, and documenting analytical decisions in R Markdown or Quarto. The course develops a repeatable workflow through modular scripts, validation checks, efficient data handling, and transparent communication of assumptions. You will create practical outputs such as a data-quality report, exploratory analysis, model diagnostic summary, and reusable analysis script while working with tools including dplyr, tidyr, data.table, broom, lme4, tidymodels, and Git-based version control concepts.
audienceIntro: R Programming for Statistical Computing is designed for professionals who use data, statistical methods, and analytical code in recurring work. It suits intermediate to advanced users who can already write basic R statements and want stronger control over analysis quality, modelling, and reproducibility.
prerequisites: You should bring a laptop with R and RStudio Desktop installed, together with permission to install packages from CRAN. The course uses instructor-provided datasets and does not require access to confidential organizational data. Basic familiarity with descriptive statistics, hypothesis testing, and linear regression will help you complete the exercises.
topics: Statistics & data analysis (SPSS, Stata, R, Python)
